associations.expansion: Skinner (2009) obtains B_u >= 0.5708858 by starting from a known lower bound B(|z|) on |f(z)| for f in class S, then using an implicit function argument to produce a tighter bound C(|z|) >= B(|z|). The implicit function arises from a nonlinear integral equation encoding distortion information. The key rigidity is that this approach cannot sharpen beyond the initial distortion estimate -- it is a one-step fixed-point improvement. To break through, one needs either a multi-step iteration of the implicit function scheme or an entirely different initial inequality.

Bonk (1990) proved B > sqrt(3)/4 using a distortion theorem for Bloch functions: Re f'(z) >= lower bound involving |z|. Refined by Chen-Gauthier (1996) and Xiong (1998) to B > sqrt(3)/4 + 3e-4. The distortion approach has a hard ceiling: it relies on Julia's Lemma and the hyperbolic metric contraction, which become loose for functions near the extremal configuration (Ahlfors-Grunsky type ramified coverings of hexagonal lattice complements).

associations.concept: Carroll-Ortega-Cerda upper bound via harmonic symmetry
associations.expansion: Carroll and Ortega-Cerda (2009) obtained the best known upper bound for B_u (approximately 0.6564) by constructing domains with threefold symmetry obtained by removing harmonically symmetric arcs from a disk. They exploit the Polya-Chebotarev problem (solved by Fedorov for 4 symmetric points) and conformal welding. The gap between 0.5709 and 0.6564 represents the current uncertainty window. The upper-bound construction suggests the extremal domain has specific rotational symmetry (likely 3-fold, matching the Ahlfors-Grunsky conjecture for B).

associations.concept: Ahlfors-Grunsky conjectured extremal and hexagonal lattice
associations.expansion: The conjectured extremal for B (and relatedly for B_u) involves universal covering maps of complements of hexagonal lattices. Baernstein and Vinson (1995) proved local minimality for the hexagonal lattice among ramified coverings over lattice points. The hexagonal lattice also appears as extremal in determinant problems for Laplace-Beltrami operators on tori (Faulhuber 2020). This deep rigidity of the hexagonal configuration may be exploitable.

The Grunsky inequalities encode necessary conditions for univalence via an infinite positive-semidefinite matrix constraint. The strong Grunsky inequality ||G|| <= 1 for schlicht functions provides a natural SDP relaxation. Truncating to finite N gives computable relaxations. Recent work by Obradovic-Tuneski (2025) shows renewed interest in Grunsky coefficient methods for sharp estimates in the general class S.

associations.concept: Kudryavtseva-Solodov program on domains of invertibility
associations.expansion: Kudryavtseva and Solodov (2019-2025) have systematically found sharp domains of univalence for self-maps of the disk with fixed points. They explicitly state that Landau's approach might be capable of delivering new lower bounds for the Bloch constant. Their work on classes B[0,{1}] with boundary and interior fixed points gives sharp covering domains that refine Landau's classical theorem, and provide tighter invertibility estimates for specific subclasses.

associations.concept: Baernstein-Eremenko-Fryntov-Solynin minimum problem for hyperbolic metrics
associations.expansion: This group (2004-2005) proved sharp covering theorems of Landau type by solving minimum problems for hyperbolic metrics on domains of the form C minus periodic sets. The key insight is that extremal configurations correspond to regular lattice-like point removal patterns. The technique of reducing covering theorems to hyperbolic metric minimum problems is the most powerful existing framework. The critical breakthrough was proving that among all domains with periodic boundary, the one with maximal symmetry (equal spacing) minimizes the hyperbolic density at the center.

The Loewner equation encodes univalent functions as time-evolving slit mappings. SLE provides a probabilistic framework. Yilin Wang's work on Loewner energy and Weil-Petersson quasicircles suggests that the extremal Bloch domain boundary may minimize a specific Loewner-Kufarev energy. The large deviations of SLE as kappa -> 0 connect to deterministic extremal problems in geometric function theory. The cutting-welding identity for Loewner energy directly parallels Carroll-Ortega-Cerda's conformal welding construction.

The conformal bootstrap (Simmons-Duffin SDPB, 2015) uses semidefinite programming to derive rigorous bounds on operator dimensions in CFTs. The structural parallel to the Bloch problem is deep: crossing symmetry constraints correspond to Grunsky/area theorem constraints, unitarity corresponds to univalence, and the gap being bounded corresponds to the inradius. The mature computational infrastructure (arbitrary-precision SDP solvers) designed for the conformal bootstrap is directly transferable. Chang-Dommes-Kravchuk-Poland-Simmons-Duffin (2025) recently developed improved approximation schemes via optimal interpolation.

associations.concept: Inradius and channel geometry at contact points
associations.expansion: The univalent Bloch constant B_u equals the infimum over normalized univalent f of the inradius of f(D). At extremal domains, the boundary makes contact with the largest inscribed disk at specific points. The geometry of the 'channels' connecting the contact points to the outer boundary determines how tight the bound is. Better understanding of channel width, taper rate, and curvature at contact points would directly improve B_u. The harmonic symmetry condition of Carroll-Ortega-Cerda constrains these channels.

associations.concept: Polya-Chebotarev problem and minimal capacity continua
associations.expansion: The problem of finding the continuum of minimal logarithmic capacity containing a given finite set is central to the upper bound construction. Schiefermayr (2013-2015) connected this to inverse polynomial images and Zolotarev conformal mappings, giving explicit solutions for symmetric configurations. This provides both computational tools and theoretical framework for optimizing domain shapes in the Bloch problem.

Beardon and Minda (2007) surveyed the hyperbolic metric and Schwarz-Pick lemma variants. Yuan-Chen-Wang (2006) strengthened the Schwarz-Pick inequality to include a correction term. For domains with specific symmetry (e.g., 3-fold), these give tighter bounds on the hyperbolic metric, which translates to tighter covering theorems. Minda (1987) specifically studied geometric function theory applications of hyperbolic metric inequalities.

associations.concept: Eremenko's hyperbolic metric on lattice complements
associations.expansion: Eremenko (2011) studied the hyperbolic metric on complements of rectangular lattices via Lame equations and accessory parameters. He attempted to prove the square lattice is extremal among rectangular lattices for the Landau problem (analogous to the hexagonal lattice being extremal among all lattices). This reduction to special function theory (Lame, Jacobi theta) provides explicit computational handles on the hyperbolic metric.

associations.concept: Faulhuber connection: Ramanujan theta functions and extremal lattices
associations.expansion: Faulhuber (2019) explicitly connected Landau's 'Weltkonstante' to heat kernels on tori and Ramanujan's theory of hypergeometric functions/elliptic modulus. He showed the restricted extremal problem (for rectangular lattices) has a solution expressible via the second lemniscate constant. This provides a potential analytical formula for the answer in the restricted lattice case.

forced_bridges.to: Grunsky matrix truncation for Bloch constant
forced_bridges.mechanism: Rewrite the Bloch constant problem as: maximize the minimum radius r such that for all univalent f with f'(0)=1, f(D) contains a disk of radius r. Express univalence via the Grunsky inequality ||G_N|| <= 1 (truncated to NxN). The Bloch constant becomes a min-max SDP: minimize over PSD Grunsky matrices, maximize inradius. Use SDPB's arbitrary-precision solver with polynomial matrix constraints. The crossing equation analogy: Grunsky coefficients play the role of OPE data, the area theorem plays the role of unitarity, and the inradius plays the role of the gap being bounded.

In the SLE framework, the boundary of the extremal Bloch domain is a curve (or union of arcs) that minimizes the Loewner-Kufarev energy subject to the constraint that the resulting domain has a given inradius. Wang's cutting-welding identity for Loewner energy connects directly to Carroll-Ortega-Cerda's conformal welding construction. The rate function of SLE_{kappa->0} gives a variational principle that should characterize the extremal domain shape. First step: compute the Loewner energy of the Carroll-Ortega-Cerda domain and verify it satisfies the Euler-Lagrange equations.

forced_bridges.from: Faulhuber extremal lattice problems (theta functions, heat kernels)
forced_bridges.to: Hexagonal lattice optimality for Bloch/Landau constant
forced_bridges.mechanism: Faulhuber proved the hexagonal lattice maximizes the Laplace-Beltrami determinant among flat tori and connected this explicitly to Landau's constant. The technique uses Ramanujan's theory of theta functions and elliptic modular properties. Bridge: express the hyperbolic metric density at the center of a fundamental domain of a lattice complement in terms of theta function ratios. The Bloch constant problem for lattice coverings then reduces to optimizing over lattice shapes, where Faulhuber's theta function machinery applies directly. The connection is: lambda_Omega(center) = 1/(conformal radius), and the Bloch constant for the lattice class is 1/max lambda_Omega.

forced_bridges.to: Improved lower bound for B_u via multi-fixed-point classes
forced_bridges.mechanism: Kudryavtseva-Solodov find sharp domains of invertibility for self-maps with constrained angular derivatives at boundary fixed points. For the Bloch problem: the extremal functions must have f'(0)=1 and be close to a Bloch function. By additionally constraining to have boundary fixed points (which the extremal should, since its image is tangent to its maximal inscribed disk), one restricts to a class where their sharp results give tighter bounds. Bridge: impose angular derivative constraints at 3 symmetrically-placed boundary points and use their sharp covering theorems on this restricted class.

forced_bridges.to: Channel geometry at extremal contact points
forced_bridges.mechanism: At extremal domains for B_u, the boundary touches the maximal inscribed disk at contact points. Formulate as optimal transport: redistribute boundary arc-length to maximize inradius subject to conformal equivalence to the disk with derivative 1 at origin. The Kantorovich dual gives a potential function on the boundary that must be constant at contact points -- this is precisely the harmonic symmetry condition of Carroll-Ortega-Cerda. This bridges the geometric optimization to the conformal analysis.

Mazac-Paulos found that extremal functionals for the 1D conformal bootstrap directly prove optimality of bounds. Transfer: find a linear functional on Taylor coefficients that is non-negative on the Grunsky cone (univalence constraint) and equals the inradius at the extremal. This would give a constructive, self-certifying lower bound. The natural basis of functionals (analogous to the GFF/GFF extremals) should be expressible via elliptic functions matching the expected hexagonal symmetry.

forced_bridges.to: Local minimality proof for B_u at conjectured extremal
forced_bridges.mechanism: Faulhuber-Steinerberger proved that among lattices of fixed density, the hexagonal lattice uniquely maximizes the 'sum of distances from far-away lattice points to the deep hole'. This has the implication that the hexagonal lattice is a strict local maximum for optimization of min-distance-type functionals. Bridge to B_u: the inradius of a lattice complement is exactly the distance from the center of a fundamental domain to the nearest lattice point. Their perturbation analysis technique (showing second-order improvement under any lattice deformation) could be adapted to prove local extremality for the Bloch problem among lattice coverings.

forced_bridges.from: Random matrix theory / Tracy-Widom edge statistics
forced_bridges.to: Spectral analysis of near-extremal Grunsky matrices
forced_bridges.mechanism: The Grunsky matrix of the extremal function (if it exists) must be near the boundary of the operator norm ball ||G|| <= 1. In RMT, matrices near the spectral edge exhibit universal behavior (Tracy-Widom). Study the spectral distribution of truncated Grunsky matrices of near-extremal functions. If the spectral distribution concentrates (as in the Tracy-Widom universality class), this gives rigid constraints on the function space that could be leveraged for analytical bounds.

anomaly_results.constraint: Restrict to univalent functions with real coefficients
anomaly_results.prediction: The 'real' univalent Bloch constant B_u^R should be strictly larger than B_u, since the real coefficient constraint eliminates rotational asymmetries. The extremal domain has bilateral symmetry about the real axis. Baernstein-Eremenko-Fryntov-Solynin's 'real Landau constant' work provides a template. Computing B_u^R would calibrate how much of the current gap is due to the difficulty of the problem vs. the loss from not exploiting symmetry.
anomaly_results.significance: If B_u^R is close to B_u, symmetry-breaking is not the main issue. If B_u^R >> B_u, the absence of symmetry constraints in current lower bound proofs is the primary bottleneck.

anomaly_results.prediction: For convex univalent functions, the inradius is at least 1/2 (by the convex Koebe theorem). The 'convex Bloch constant' is exactly 1/2. This degenerate case reveals that the extremal for B_u must have a highly non-convex image with narrow channels doubling back near contact points.
anomaly_results.significance: Establishes that non-convexity of the image is essential, pointing to the channel geometry as the critical geometric feature.

anomaly_results.constraint: Impose n-fold symmetry on the domain for varying n = 1,2,3,4,6
anomaly_results.prediction: B_u^(1) = B_u (no constraint). B_u^(2) > B_u (bilateral symmetry helps). B_u^(3) should be close to the true B_u if the Ahlfors-Grunsky conjecture is correct. B_u^(6) > B_u^(3) (over-constraining). The sequence B_u^(n) is monotonically non-decreasing. Computing B_u^(3) vs B_u^(6) tests whether 3-fold or 6-fold symmetry is the right ansatz.
anomaly_results.significance: Directly tests the symmetry conjecture. If B_u^(3) = B_u^(6), the extremal has 6-fold symmetry; if B_u^(3) < B_u^(6), the extremal has exactly 3-fold symmetry.

anomaly_results.prediction: Starlike B_u should be computable via subordination theory and strictly larger than B_u. The gap quantifies the role of non-starlike geometry (channels that wind around the inscribed disk).
anomaly_results.significance: If the gap is small, the Bloch extremal is nearly starlike and perturbative methods from the starlike class might work. If the gap is large, the extremal is fundamentally non-starlike.

anomaly_results.constraint: Allow derivative normalization |f'(0)|=1 but not f(0)=0 (Landau constant L vs B_u)
anomaly_results.prediction: L >= B_u is known. The conjectured values differ. Studying L - B_u as a function of |f(0)| reveals how translation symmetry interacts with the Bloch property. At |f(0)| = 0, we recover B_u. As |f(0)| increases, the covering radius should change monotonically.
anomaly_results.significance: The Landau problem is analytically richer (the center of the covered disk is a free variable). Understanding the relationship constrains the geometry of the Bloch extremal.

anomaly_results.constraint: Non-univalent Bloch constant B vs univalent B_u
anomaly_results.prediction: B < B_u since non-univalent functions can have branch points that reduce the schlicht disk radius. The current best lower bound for B is sqrt(3)/4 + 3e-4 (Xiong 1998). Understanding where univalence adds value (how much B_u exceeds B) reveals which parts of Skinner/Bonk analyses genuinely use univalence vs merely the Bloch condition.
anomaly_results.significance: If B_u - B is large, univalence provides substantial leverage that current proofs under-exploit.

anomaly_results.constraint: Higher dimensions: Bloch constant for B^n -> C^n
anomaly_results.prediction: Lower bounds degrade rapidly with dimension (Hamada-Kohr). If the SDP/Grunsky approach works in 1D, it may generalize to higher dimensions where the problem is more open, providing a proof-of-concept.
anomaly_results.significance: High-dimensional success would validate the SDP methodology before applying to the harder 1D precision problem.

anomaly_results.constraint: Use quasihyperbolic metric instead of hyperbolic metric
anomaly_results.prediction: The quasihyperbolic metric k_D(z) = |dz|/dist(z, bdry D) approximates the hyperbolic metric with k_D <= 2*lambda_D for simply connected domains. Working with k_D gives looser but more explicit and computable bounds. The quasihyperbolic inradius provides a tractable proxy (Koskela 1998).
anomaly_results.significance: If quasihyperbolic bounds come close to the hyperbolic ones, the additional complexity of exact hyperbolic metric computation is unnecessary.

steering_directions.direction: SDP relaxation via truncated Grunsky matrix
steering_directions.rationale: The Grunsky inequality provides a convex (PSD) constraint encoding univalence. Truncating to NxN gives a finite SDP whose optimal value provides a rigorous lower bound on B_u. As N -> infinity, the bound converges to B_u. This completely bypasses Skinner's implicit function approach and directly optimizes the inradius. The conformal bootstrap community has mature SDP solvers (SDPB) designed for exactly this type of problem.
steering_directions.first_step: Formulate the inradius of f(D) in terms of the Taylor/Grunsky coefficients. For f(z) = z + a_2*z^2 + ..., express the condition that disk D(w_0, r) is contained in f(D) via coefficient constraints. Write: maximize r subject to ||G_N|| <= 1, |f'(0)|=1. Implement using SDPB or MOSEK. Start with N=5 and increase.
steering_directions.expected_signal: For N=10-20, the SDP should give a lower bound competitive with or exceeding 0.5709. If at N=50 the bound exceeds 0.58, the approach will likely reach the conjectured value with sufficient computation. If the bound plateaus well below 0.6564, additional constraints beyond Grunsky are needed.

steering_directions.rationale: The Baernstein-Eremenko approach reduces Bloch/Landau bounds to minimum problems for hyperbolic metrics. For B_u, the conjectured extremal has 3-fold symmetry. Imposing this reduces to a 1-parameter family of domains. The hyperbolic metric on such domains can be computed via elliptic functions (Eremenko 2011 approach via Lame equations).
steering_directions.first_step: Parameterize 3-fold symmetric domains of Carroll-Ortega-Cerda type: D minus three symmetric arcs. Compute the hyperbolic metric at the origin using the Schwarz-Christoffel Toolbox (Driscoll-Trefethen) or via Lame equations. Minimize the conformal radius over the arc parameter family.
steering_directions.expected_signal: If the minimum conformal radius matches ~0.6564, the extremal has 3-fold symmetry. If strictly larger, the extremal breaks 3-fold symmetry. Either way, this pins down the symmetry class.

steering_directions.direction: Kudryavtseva-Solodov multi-fixed-point refinement of Landau's approach
steering_directions.rationale: Kudryavtseva-Solodov (2022-2025) explicitly suggest their approach can deliver new Bloch constant bounds. Their sharp results for B[0,{1}] classes (self-maps with interior and boundary fixed points) give tighter invertibility estimates than classical Landau when additional fixed-point structure is known.
steering_directions.first_step: Take f in the normalized Bloch class. Let g(z) = f(z)/(2M) for suitable M, mapping D into D with g(0)=0, g'(0) = 1/(2M). Identify boundary fixed-point structure of g. Apply Kudryavtseva-Solodov's invertibility theorem to get a covering disk for g, then rescale to get a covering disk for f. Compare numerically with 0.5709.
steering_directions.expected_signal: If their sharp bound exceeds Skinner's for the relevant parameter values, this gives an immediate improvement with existing theory. The key check is whether the angular derivative constraints at boundary fixed points provide enough leverage.

steering_directions.direction: Loewner-energy variational characterization of extremal domain
steering_directions.rationale: Wang's Loewner energy provides a potential on Jordan curves. The extremal domain boundary for B_u should be a critical point of Loewner energy subject to an inradius constraint. This gives E-L equations that characterize the extremal. If solvable (even numerically), this identifies the extremal domain and closes the gap.
steering_directions.first_step: Formulate the constrained optimization: minimize inradius(f(D)) over f in S, parameterized by Loewner driving function. Express Loewner energy as integral of driving function squared. Derive E-L equations. Check whether the Carroll-Ortega-Cerda domain satisfies them.
steering_directions.expected_signal: Unique solution with 3-fold symmetry matching conjectured extremal provides strong support. If Carroll-Ortega-Cerda domain does NOT satisfy E-L equations, a new domain shape is predicted.

steering_directions.rationale: Bypass analytical difficulties entirely. Parameterize univalent functions by truncated Taylor series or Loewner driving functions. Compute inradius numerically. Minimize over parameter space using gradient-based optimization. This gives a numerical lower bound and identifies near-extremal domain shapes.
steering_directions.first_step: Implement: given Taylor coefficients (a_2,...,a_N), evaluate f on boundary grid, compute inradius via Chebyshev center problem, check univalence via argument principle. Optimize using CMA-ES or L-BFGS-B. Start with N=10 polynomial truncation.
steering_directions.expected_signal: Optimizer converges to domain with approximate 3-fold symmetry. Inradius near 0.6564 confirms Carroll-Ortega-Cerda upper bound is tight from below. Domain shape reveals channel geometry at contact points.

steering_directions.direction: Transfer analytic functional bootstrap to Bloch problem
steering_directions.rationale: Mazac-Paulos extremal functionals directly prove optimality of bootstrap bounds. Transfer: find a linear functional on Taylor coefficients that is non-negative on the Grunsky cone and equals the inradius at the extremal. This gives a constructive, self-certifying lower bound.
steering_directions.first_step: Study the dual SDP formulation: dual variables form a positive kernel K(z,w) such that B_u equals the minimum of a linear functional over K satisfying positivity and Grunsky constraints. Implement dual SDP for small truncation sizes (N=5-10). Extract and analyze the extremal functional.
steering_directions.expected_signal: Clean analytic form for the extremal functional suggests an analytical proof is possible. Messy functional suggests purely numerical methods are needed. Either way, the dual gives rigorous bounds.

validation_checks.direction: SDP relaxation via truncated Grunsky matrix
checks: Verify SDP reproduces Koebe 1/4 bound at N=1 (area theorem only)
Check monotonicity: bound at N+1 >= bound at N
Compare with Skinner's 0.5709 at moderate N (10-20)
Verify extremal SDP solution yields valid Grunsky matrix (eigenvalues in [-1,1])
Cross-check: extremal Taylor coefficients define approximately univalent function (verify via argument principle on numerical evaluation)
Check that the SDP dual value matches primal (strong duality verification)
Verify Schwarz-Christoffel computation: for full disk (no arcs), conformal radius at origin = 1
For slit disk, compare with known closed-form formulas
Check Lame equation approach reproduces Eremenko (2011) results for rectangular lattices
Verify conformal radius is continuous and differentiable in arc parameters
Check critical point of family matches Carroll-Ortega-Cerda domain parameters
Verify hyperbolic density computation against Beardon-Minda tables for standard domains
Verify their theorem reproduces Landau's classical result when boundary fixed-point constraint is removed
Check that composed function g = f/(2M) belongs to class B[0] with correct derivative constraint
Compare covering disk radius from their theorem with Skinner bound for same normalization
Test on Koebe function: k(z) = z/(1-z)^2 should give covering disk exactly 1/4
Verify the angular derivative constraint at boundary point is compatible with the Bloch normalization
Verify Loewner energy computation: energy of circle = 0, energy of slit domain computable via driving function
Check E-L derivation by verifying first-order optimality at conjectured extremal
Verify small perturbations of Carroll-Ortega-Cerda domain increase inradius (local minimum of inradius = local max of Bloch)
Cross-check: the Loewner driving function of the conjectured extremal should have specific symmetry properties (period-3)
Verify inradius computation: f(z)=z gives inradius 1, Koebe function gives inradius 1/4
Check optimizer finds minimum consistent with B_u >= 0.5709
Verify imposing 3-fold symmetry does not change minimum (tests symmetry conjecture)
Confirm near-extremal domain has expected qualitative features: narrow channels, contact points on inscribed disk
Check convergence: increasing N in polynomial truncation should give monotonically decreasing minimum inradius
Verify dual SDP is well-posed (strong duality holds)
Check dual optimal value matches primal optimal value
Verify extremal functional satisfies positivity on test set of univalent functions
Check whether extremal functional is expressible as rational function of spectral parameter (as in GFF bootstrap case)
Verify that the functional certifies the known Koebe 1/4 bound for the simplest truncation
